Here's the outcome list, built from the spec's requirements. I haven't written any roadmap text yet; it waits on your ranking.

## Outcomes (unranked)

| # | Outcome | From | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | One archived quarter's filing index as a canonical Parquet catalog, built from raw bytes kept in storage | R1, R3, R6 | 2–3 SEC requests (listing + file); data volume measured by the first run |
| O2 | A baseline catalog over a quarter range you choose, with a per-source complete / pending / failed report and no silent gaps | R1, §4.2 | Range not set yet (§4.8). For 1993–2026, about 136 quarters and roughly 300 requests, under 2 min of request budget at 3 req/s. Bytes unknown. The larger cost is your time on golden fixtures for each historical format in the range (§4.6), unknown until the formats are seen |
| O3 | Daily indexes added to the catalog, catching up after missed runs and across quarter boundaries | R2 | About 250 daily files a year plus a few listings per run; small in requests and bytes |
| O4 | The catalog rebuilt after a parser change from stored bytes, with no SEC requests and no duplicate records | R6 | No SEC cost; compute about one O2 transform pass, measured |
| O5 | Weekly reconciliation: SEC corrections to quarterly indexes applied, withdrawals held until you approve the exact source hash | R7, R10 | Re-downloads every supported quarter weekly (about the same requests as O2), plus your time per approval, frequency unknown |
| O6 | All SEC traffic from every run kept under one 3 req/s budget, with an identifying User-Agent and the stated retry limits | R8, R11 | No external cost |
| O7 | Readers see only complete quarter generations through one active pointer; a crash never leaves half-published data | R9, §4.6 | No external cost |
| O8 | A failed run resumes where it stopped, reusing completed sources | §1, §4.7 | No external cost |
| O9 | The system running on Azure (ADF, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS, Table Storage), with triggers disabled until release | R4 | Azure dollars can't be estimated before resource sizing; the spec's smoke test (§7 step 4) measures it |
| O10 | Alerts, run reports and runbooks for operations: throttling, approvals, replay, rollback | §4.7, §8 | Log Analytics ingestion, small; measured |
| O11 | Scheduled operation accepted on observed scheduled runs | §7 steps 6–9 | At least one week of calendar time to observe a weekly reconciliation |

## Track

**A — SEC filing-index catalog (known progression)**, all eleven outcomes. I considered splitting the Azure outcomes (O9–O11) into their own track. They don't stand without the catalog, though, so that is a dependency, not a separate question. One track it is, unless you see a different use I'm missing.

## Choices already made

- Python 3.14, uv workspace (repo).
- Azure platform per the ADR (R4). The ADR is still *Proposed*; I'm treating its choice as made.
- One shared downloader, parser and publisher for backfill, daily and reconciliation (R5).
- §4.8's starting defaults (R11).
- The code goes in `packages/sec-edgar-ingest` (§4.9). The spec doesn't mention the other three scaffold packages.

Roadmap file: `specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md` (the spec's stem).

**Optional probe:** to firm up the byte costs for O1 and O2, I could fetch the `full-index` listings for one recent quarter and for 1993 Q1. SEC requires an identifying User-Agent, so I'd need the string you want to use.

**Please rank O1–O11 by value to you, and confirm the single known-progression track (or change it).**
